ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: Image description: The figure shows a two-transistor Schmitt trigger circuit, the power supply is +5 V, the collector of the right-side transistor is connected to +5 V through a resistor labeled 200Ω, and the output terminal Vo is taken directly from the collector of this right-side transistor. The emitters of the two transistors are connected to a common node, and this node is grounded through a 1kΩ resistor; the current I=1.25 mA is marked in this branch in the figure. Reasoning: When the output is logic low, according to the method specified in the problem, it is identified that the right-side transistor is saturated, because Vo is located at the collector of the right-side transistor. The common emitter voltage is obtained from the emitter resistor current marked in the figure: VE = I × R = 1.25 mA × 1 kΩ = 1.25 V. When saturated, the right-side transistor satisfies VCE(sat)=VC−VE=0.1 V, therefore the output low level VOL=VC=VE+VCE(sat)=1.25 V+0.1 V=1.35 V.
